title: Salwa and the Stony Ground
logline: Salwa plants a hidden seed in Nour, the hardest ground of all.
story: Nothing had ever grown in Nour, who was light (the city's intrinsic light) — ground so hard the others laughed when Salwa, who carried journeying horsewoman, seeker of unity, was handed a single seed and told to plant it there. Salwa did not argue; Salwa simply returned each day to tend the barren place. No green came for a long season, and still Salwa watered the stone. Then one morning a thread of root had split the rock from within. What force could not break, patience had quietly opened.
moral: What force cannot break, steady and patient tending opens from within.
attribution: a Pagarek parable, from Project Genesis
